summary: Daniel Dubuisson specializes in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at University Lille-III and served as director of research at both CNRS and the University of Lille (attested 2010).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard, with W. V. O. Quine, Walter Eugene Clark, and Kalipada Tarkacharya. He was a Junior Fellow (1939) and Wales Professor of Sanskrit (~1958-1983) at Harvard.

Daniel John Gogerly was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He ran the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818-1834), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (1838), and held leadership posts at the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1858-1862).

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Westmar, Garrett-Evangelical, and Chicago under Philip Kuhn, Mircea Eliade, and Joseph Kitagawa, he spent his career at the University of British Columbia (~1973-2000; emeritus ~1973-2001).

Daniel M. Stuart works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, mentored by Alexander von Rospatt, and served as Assistant Professor at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017).

Daniel M. Veidlinger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins. He held posts at Chiang Mai University (1999) and California State University, Chico (attested 2006).
Daniel P. Brown was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ngawang Wangyal. He served as a professor at Harvard University.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he was advised by Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel S. Capper works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Schlumberger was a historian and archaeologist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1923-1925) and held a post at Princeton University (~1966-1967).

Daniel Sperber works in history and archaeology. He studied at Kol Torah, Yeshivah of Flatbush, Kilburn Grammar School, and University College London (~1965-1968). His academic posts include Bar-Ilan University (~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under Jay L. Garfield, also studying with Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Virginia, where he served as an instructor (attested 2010), while also teaching at Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).

Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned a PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology at the University of Siena and was a fellow at the Centre d'Etudes Himalayennes (attested 2004).

Daniela Bevilacqua works in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and served as a post-doctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
Danielle Feller is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne (until 2001) under Johannes Bronkhorst, also studying under Ganesh U. Thite.

Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920-1924) and with Jacques Bacot (~1934-1937), later serving as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China (~1953-1992).

Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He held positions at Hindu College, the University of Delhi (~1957-1967), Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and as Director of the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute.

Daud Ali specializes in Indology and history. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (~1999-2009) before joining the University of Pennsylvania as associate professor in 2009.

Dave Tomlinson works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2019) under Dan Arnold, also studying under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.
